title: MCP Apps: Extending the Frontier — Ido Salomon & Liad Yosef

primary.label: Tools, Protocols & Integrations
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 98%).

domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: MCP Apps is fundamentally a tool and protocol for software builders who create MCP servers and integrate them with hosts. The talk addresses SDKs, repos, and the developer ecosystem directly.

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: MCP Apps is a cross-domain standard designed to work across any application vertical—from e-commerce (Shopify) to analytics (PostHog) to creative tools. The agentic web vision is explicitly domain-agnostic.

domains.label: Coding Assistants
domains.rationale: Several adopting hosts are coding assistants (VS Code, Cursor, Copilot), and the talk demonstrates MCP Apps running in these environments. However, the standard is broader than coding assistants alone.

domains.label: Personal Productivity
domains.rationale: The agentic web vision describes personal assistants composing UI atoms from multiple services (calendar, shopping, booking) for individual productivity tasks. This is a forward-looking vision rather than the current primary use case.

summary: This talk by Ido Salomon and Liad Yosef at the AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 introduces MCP Apps, the first official extension to the Model Context Protocol (SEP-1865), which enables MCP servers to return interactive HTML UIs instead of plain text. The speakers explain that text is the worst medium for conveying rich information and that companies resist building MCP servers because they fear losing brand identity and being reduced to a textual database. The solution: MCP servers send UI chunks—HTML resources linked from tool calls—that hosts render as web components in sandboxed iframes, with user interactions flowing back into the agentic loop via callbacks. Liad created the precursor project MCP-UI in May 2025; it was later formalized as MCP Apps through partnership with Anthropic and OpenAI. The spec is now adopted by Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor, Copilot, and GitHub, with OpenAI recommending MCP Apps for building ChatGPT apps. A live PostHog demo shows an interactive funnel widget rendered in Claude. The talk covers the architecture (tool call to resource to sandboxed web component to callback to tool call), the agentic web vision where websites decompose into UI atoms composed by personal assistants, three levels of app-to-chat control (notify, request prompt, release full responsibility), upcoming features (reusable views, view tools, generative UI spectrum), and interoperability with Google's A2UI declarative UI standard. The distribution argument emphasizes 800 million weekly ChatGPT users giving developers 170x the Apple App Store's launch TAM. A tri-weekly working group within the MCP committee continues evolving the spec.
whyItMatters: The software engineering and AI concepts in this talk form a coherent stack: the Model Context Protocol provides the transport layer, MCP Apps (SEP-1865) extends it with the ui:// URI scheme and tool-to-resource linking to deliver interactive HTML, sandboxed iframe rendering provides the security boundary, and JSON-RPC callbacks close the agentic loop by feeding user interactions back to the model. On the AI side, the agentic web vision and UI atoms composition represent the target state this protocol enables, while the generative UI spectrum and A2UI interoperability show how MCP Apps fits into the broader landscape of UI delivery paradigms. The three levels of app-to-chat control and host-mediated control flow ensure that this richer interaction model remains safe and auditable. Together, these concepts describe how a community open-source project (MCP-UI) was formalized into an official protocol extension that transforms MCP servers from text-returning APIs into rich UI providers, with write-once-run-anywhere portability across the major AI platforms that collectively reach hundreds of millions of users.
temporalContext: The talk was published on 2026-08-02 and presented at the AI Engineer World's Fair 2026. MCP-UI was created in May 2025 as a community project. MCP Apps was formally proposed as SEP-1865 on 2025-11-21 and announced as the first official MCP extension with a stable specification on 2026-01-26. The A2UI interoperability guide was published on 2026-06-17. As of the research date (2026-08-23), the spec continues evolving through a tri-weekly working group, with reusable views and view tools described as upcoming but not yet released. The speakers noted the talk itself might already be out of date due to rapid spec evolution. The video was researched approximately three weeks after publication.

MCP Apps lets servers return interactive HTML UI that hosts render as sandboxed web components, with user clicks flowing back into the agentic loop via callbacks

concepts.name: Generative UI spectrum
concepts.explanation: A spectrum spanning predefined UI (MCP Apps returns fixed HTML), declarative UI (JSON render, A2UI where the host interprets a JSON description), and fully generative UI (the model generates UI on the fly). MCP Apps positions itself across this spectrum.
concepts.importance: Frames the design space for UI delivery in agentic systems; helps developers choose the right level of flexibility vs. control for their use case.

concepts.name: Agentic web
concepts.explanation: A vision where websites decompose into small UI atoms (chunks) that personal assistants compose dynamically. Instead of users navigating 20 separate websites, the assistant pulls relevant UI chunks from multiple services with full context.
concepts.importance: The overarching vision that MCP Apps enables; represents a paradigm shift from browser-based web consumption to assistant-mediated UI composition.

concepts.name: Agentic loop with UI callbacks
concepts.explanation: The cycle where a user prompt triggers a tool call, the tool returns a UI resource, the host renders it, user interactions generate callbacks, and the model issues further tool calls to advance the conversation.
concepts.importance: Core interaction model that distinguishes MCP Apps from traditional API responses; integrates human UI interaction into the agent reasoning loop.

concepts.name: A2UI interoperability
concepts.explanation: Google's A2UI is a declarative UI protocol for Gemini. An interoperability guide (co-authored by the speakers and published on Google Developers Blog) explains how a server can write A2UI for Gemini and wrap it as an MCP App for ChatGPT, and vice versa.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates cross-platform UI standard interoperability; allows developers to target multiple AI hosts with minimal adaptation.

concepts.name: Claude's generative UI built on MCP Apps
concepts.explanation: Claude's generate-UI feature, which produces interactive HTML explanations on the fly, is itself built on the MCP Apps protocol behind the scenes.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates that MCP Apps is not just a theoretical spec but already powers production generative UI features in a major AI product.

concepts.name: Host-mediated control flow
concepts.explanation: In the MCP Apps architecture, the host (chat client) retains control over all actions. Apps cannot autonomously call backends; they recommend tool calls to the host, which decides whether to execute them. This ensures auditability and user control.
concepts.importance: Safety and governance model that prevents rogue app behavior; the host acts as a gatekeeper for all agent actions.

concepts.name: MCP server as UI provider
concepts.explanation: Traditionally MCP servers expose tools and return text. With MCP Apps, servers become UI providers, returning branded interactive components that preserve company identity within the chat interface.
concepts.importance: Solves the adoption barrier where companies resisted MCP servers due to loss of brand identity; transforms servers from text APIs into rich UI platforms.

concepts.name: UI atoms composition by personal assistants
concepts.explanation: The concept that complex websites will fragment into individual UI components (atoms) that AI personal assistants dynamically compose based on user intent, pulling from Google Calendar, Amazon, Booking, etc. with full conversational context.
concepts.importance: Represents the future state of web interaction mediated by AI; MCP Apps provides the protocol substrate for this decomposition.

concepts.name: Cross-host AI platform distribution
concepts.explanation: MCP Apps enables developers to reach users across multiple AI platforms (ChatGPT with 800M weekly users, Claude, VS Code, Cursor, Copilot) through a single integration, creating a distribution channel with 170x the Apple App Store's launch TAM.
concepts.importance: Frames MCP Apps as not just a protocol but a distribution platform; the scale argument drives adoption incentives for developers.

concepts.name: Declarative UI (JSON render, A2UI)
concepts.explanation: A UI paradigm where the server sends a JSON description of the UI rather than full HTML. The host interprets the JSON and renders native components. A2UI is Google's implementation of this for Gemini.
concepts.importance: Part of the generative UI spectrum; offers a middle ground between fixed HTML and fully generative UI, with cross-host portability advantages.

concepts.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
concepts.explanation: An open standard protocol that defines how AI applications connect to external data sources and tools via a client-server architecture using JSON-RPC. MCP Apps is an official extension to this protocol.
concepts.importance: Foundational protocol that the entire talk builds upon; MCP Apps extends it with interactive UI delivery capabilities.

concepts.name: MCP Apps (SEP-1865)
concepts.explanation: The first official MCP extension, standardized as SEP-1865 with Final status, enabling servers to deliver interactive HTML user interfaces to hosts via the ui:// URI scheme and tool-to-resource linking.
concepts.importance: The primary subject of the talk; defines the protocol mechanics for returning interactive UI instead of text from MCP servers.

concepts.name: Tool-to-resource linking
concepts.explanation: An MCP tool call includes metadata (_meta.ui.resourceUri) that points to an HTML resource (ui:// URI). The host fetches and renders that resource instead of displaying a text response.
concepts.importance: Core architectural mechanism that enables UI delivery; links the existing MCP resource primitive to interactive rendering.

concepts.name: Sandboxed iframe rendering
concepts.explanation: Hosts render MCP App HTML inside sandboxed iframes with declarative Content Security Policy, isolating the app from the host while allowing bidirectional communication.
concepts.importance: Security boundary that makes it safe for hosts to render arbitrary server-provided HTML; essential for the trust model of the protocol.

concepts.name: Callback-based interaction flow
concepts.explanation: When users interact with a rendered MCP App (e.g., clicking a button), the app sends a message to the host recommending a tool call rather than calling the backend directly. The host retains control and decides whether to execute the tool call.
concepts.importance: Preserves host control over the agentic loop; the app cannot autonomously execute actions, which is critical for safety and auditability.

concepts.name: JSON-RPC bidirectional communication
concepts.explanation: MCP Apps uses JSON-RPC over postMessage for bidirectional communication between the rendered app and the host, enabling callbacks and host-to-app messaging.
concepts.importance: Defines the wire protocol for app-host communication; essential for implementing the callback flow and view tools.

concepts.name: Write-once-run-anywhere portability
concepts.explanation: The same MCP app codebase runs across all supporting hosts (Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor, Libre Chat) without modification, similar to how web standards enable cross-browser compatibility.
concepts.importance: Core value proposition for developers; eliminates the need to build separate integrations for each host platform.

concepts.name: Multi-language SDK packages
concepts.explanation: The MCP-UI and ext-apps SDKs provide packages in TypeScript (@mcp-ui/client, @mcp-ui/server, @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps), Python, and Ruby for building MCP Apps servers and host integrations.
concepts.importance: Practical tooling that enables developers to implement the protocol across different technology stacks.

concepts.name: Reusable views
concepts.explanation: An upcoming spec feature that allows an MCP App to persist its rendered view across conversation turns without re-rendering, using identifiers passed from the server so the host can update the same view instead of creating a new one.
concepts.importance: Solves the performance problem for heavy apps (e.g., Autodesk's 3D renderer) that would otherwise re-render on every turn; critical for complex interactive applications.

concepts.name: View tools / app tools
concepts.explanation: A spec feature standardizing host-to-app communication, allowing the host to send messages to the rendered app (e.g., auto-filling a form for the user), complementing the existing app-to-host callback flow.
concepts.importance: Enables bidirectional control; the host can manipulate the app's state, which is essential for agentic workflows where the assistant drives UI changes.

concepts.name: Three levels of app-to-chat control
concepts.explanation: MCP Apps standardizes three control levels: (1) notify the chat of an event, (2) request prompt execution by the model, (3) release full responsibility to the host. No single app controls the user journey; everything flows through the chat for auditability.
concepts.importance: Defines the governance model for how apps interact with the agentic loop; critical for safety, auditability, and user control.

concepts.name: ui:// URI scheme
concepts.explanation: A URI scheme introduced by SEP-1865 for declaring UI resources within the MCP resource system. Tool calls reference ui:// resources that hosts fetch and render as interactive HTML.
concepts.importance: The addressing mechanism that integrates UI resources into the existing MCP resource primitive; enables discovery and retrieval of UI content.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Ido Salomon and Liad Yosef introduce themselves. Ido is co-creator and maintainer of MCP apps on the MCP steering committee. Liad is co-creator of the MCP apps spec and recently co-founded Aura, a research lab for the agentic web.

sections.title: Why we need MCP Apps
sections.summary: MCP apps are already present in ChatGPT, VS Code, and Slack. Text is the worst way to convey rich information. Companies resist building MCP servers because they don't want to be reduced to a textual database or lose their brand identity. The proposed solution: apps send their own UI chunks into the chat.

sections.title: From walls of text to interactive views
sections.summary: Instead of textual responses, apps could send branded UI into the chat—Shopify, Hugging Face, Monday—so users recognize brands at a glance. The goal extends beyond visualization to full interactivity, letting users interact with embedded apps like Hugging Face directly.

sections.title: MCP UI, created and adopted
sections.summary: Liad created MCP UI in May of the prior year as an open protocol for interactive applications over MCP, covering both UI transmission and host communication. They later partnered with Anthropic and OpenAI to create MCP Apps as the official extension. Early adopters include 11 Labs, Shopify, Postman, and Goose. Block released an agentic commerce solution based on MCP Apps. Current supporters include Claude, VS Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot, and GitHub. OpenAI recommends MCP Apps for building ChatGPT apps.

sections.title: An open working group in the MCP committee
sections.summary: A public repo accepts PRs and proposals for extending the spec. A working group in the MCP committee meets tri-weekly with Anthropic, OpenAI, and partners to shape the protocol for both large apps and the broader community. A growing community builds plugins, integrations, and courses around MCP Apps.

sections.title: How a tool call becomes an interface
sections.summary: Core concept: instead of returning text, an MCP server returns HTML via an existing resource primitive. Hosts that support MCP Apps render that HTML as an interactive application. When users click (e.g., a favorite button), the app sends a message to the host rather than the backend, recommending a tool call. The host retains control of the flow and decides whether to call the tool.

sections.title: Standardizing the flow (PostHog demo)
sections.summary: Live demo in Claude: a product manager asks about funnel status. Instead of a useless textual response from PostHog, MCP Apps returns a branded, interactive PostHog widget. The user can click a funnel step to send a prompt back to the model for explanation, advancing the agentic flow interactively.

sections.title: The architecture: resources and web components
sections.summary: Architecture flow: prompt to tool call linked to a resource, host consumes the HTML resource, MCP UI SDK renders it as a React or web component in a sandbox, accepting the resource plus a callback. User clicks send events back through the callback; the model can issue tool calls or fetch resources to complete the agentic loop.

sections.title: Consuming apps through the browser (agentic web vision)
sections.summary: The vision: instead of consuming the web through browser tabs, personal assistants compose UI atoms from multiple services. Planning an anniversary no longer requires conveying intent to 20 separate UIs—the assistant pulls relevant chunks (Google Calendar, Amazon, Booking) with full context. MCP Apps standardizes three levels of control: apps notify the chat, request prompt execution, or release full responsibility to the chat host. No single app controls the user journey; everything flows through the chat for auditability.

sections.title: What's still evolving in the spec
sections.summary: The spec continues to evolve with community contributions. The official SDK is maintained directly so spec changes are immediately reflected. Upcoming features include reusable views (so heavy apps like Autodesk's 3D renderer don't re-render on every turn), app tools or view tools (letting the host speak to the app, e.g., auto-filling a form for the user), and a generative UI spectrum spanning predefined UI (MCP Apps), declarative UI (JSON render, A2UI), and fully generative UI. Claude's generate-UI feature is built on MCP Apps behind the scenes.

sections.title: Interoperability across hosts
sections.summary: A guide released days before the talk explains how a server can write A2UI for Gemini and wrap it as an MCP app for ChatGPT and vice versa. The same MCP app codebase runs in both Libre Chat (open source) and ChatGPT, demonstrating write-once-run-anywhere.

sections.title: Write once, reach hundreds of millions
sections.summary: The distribution argument: ChatGPT has 800 million weekly users (~10% of the world population), compared to 13 years for the web to reach that number. MCP Apps gives developers 170x the total addressable market of the Apple App Store at launch. The speakers encourage the audience to visit the official repo, embrace the new web, and contribute to the spec.

organization.name: Model Context Protocol
organization.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol established as 'Model Context Protocol, a Series of LF Projects, LLC.' It uses a hierarchical governance model (Contributors, Maintainers, Core Maintainers, Lead Maintainers) similar to Python and PyTorch. Lead Maintainers are Justin Spahr-Summers and David Soria Parra. All maintainers form the MCP Steering Group. MCP Apps (SEP-1865) is its first official extension, enabling interactive UI delivery over the protocol. The spec was finalized on 2026-01-26 with a draft version in active development.
organization.status: Active — open source project under LF Projects, LLC with formal governance; MCP Apps spec stable as of 2026-01-26 with draft version in active development

technologies.label: MCP Apps (SEP-1865) — Interactive UI Protocol Extension
technologies.summary: MCP Apps is the first official extension to the Model Context Protocol, standardized as SEP-1865 with Final status. It enables MCP servers to deliver interactive HTML user interfaces to hosts instead of plain text responses. The architecture works as follows: an MCP tool call includes metadata (_meta.ui.resourceUri) pointing to a ui:// HTML resource; the host fetches and renders that resource in a sandboxed iframe; user interactions generate JSON-RPC callbacks over postMessage that recommend tool calls to the host; the host retains control and decides whether to execute them, closing the agentic loop. The spec standardizes three levels of app-to-chat control (notify, request prompt execution, release full responsibility) for governance and auditability. Upcoming features include reusable views (persisting rendered views across turns for heavy apps) and view tools (host-to-app communication for actions like auto-filling forms). Adopted by Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor, Copilot, and GitHub, with OpenAI recommending MCP Apps for building ChatGPT apps. The spec continues evolving through a tri-weekly working group within the MCP committee.
technologies.role: Primary subject of the talk; the entire presentation explains the motivation, architecture, adoption, and future evolution of MCP Apps as a protocol extension

technologies.label: MCP-UI — Precursor SDK Project
technologies.summary: MCP-UI is the open-source precursor project created by Ido Salomon in collaboration with Liad Yosef in May 2025, which pioneered the pattern of delivering interactive UI over the Model Context Protocol. Its architectural patterns—HTML resources returned from tool calls, sandboxed rendering, and bidirectional communication—directly influenced and were formalized into the MCP Apps specification (SEP-1865) through partnership with Anthropic and OpenAI. The project maintains multi-language SDK packages (TypeScript, Python, Ruby) for both server-side UI delivery and host-side rendering, including AppRenderer and UIResourceRenderer components for host integration. The mcpui.dev site serves as the project's documentation hub.
technologies.role: Origin project and SDK provider; Liad Yosef describes creating MCP-UI in May of the prior year, and the speakers explain how its patterns were formalized into the official MCP Apps extension through partnership with Anthropic and OpenAI

technologies.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP) — Foundational Protocol
technologies.summary: The Model Context Protocol is the open standard protocol defining how AI applications connect to external data sources and tools via a client-server architecture using JSON-RPC. MCP Apps is the first official extension to this protocol, building on MCP's existing resource and tool primitives to deliver interactive UI. The protocol is maintained by the modelcontextprotocol organization and governed through a Standards Extension Proposal (SEP) process, with a steering committee that includes the talk's speakers. The tri-weekly working group within the MCP committee continues to shape the spec with Anthropic, OpenAI, and community partners.
technologies.role: Foundational protocol that MCP Apps extends; the talk assumes familiarity with MCP concepts (tools, resources) and explains how MCP Apps reuses these primitives for UI delivery

technologies.label: A2UI — Declarative UI Interoperability
technologies.summary: A2UI is Google's declarative UI protocol for Gemini, representing the declarative UI point on the generative UI spectrum discussed in the talk. An interoperability guide co-authored by Ido Salomon and Liad Yosef and published on the Google Developers Blog on 2026-06-17 explains how a server can write A2UI for Gemini and wrap it as an MCP App for ChatGPT, and vice versa. This interoperability demonstrates that MCP Apps is part of a broader ecosystem of UI delivery standards spanning predefined UI (MCP Apps HTML), declarative UI (A2UI, JSON render), and fully generative UI (model-generated UI). The same MCP app codebase has been demonstrated running in both Libre Chat (open source) and ChatGPT, proving the write-once-run-anywhere portability claim.
technologies.role: Interoperability counterpart to MCP Apps in the generative UI spectrum; the talk presents A2UI as part of the broader landscape of UI delivery paradigms and demonstrates cross-host portability

resources.title: Liad Yosef - MCP Dev Summit North America
resources.why: Verifies Liad Yosef's identity and role. Notes he was previously AI Lead in Shopify's CEO office and is co-founder/CTO at a company (listed as 'Ora' on the conference page, while the transcript says 'Aura' — the organization name is uncertain).

resources.title: MCP-UI Creators on Why AI Agents Need Rich User Interfaces
resources.why: Confirms the May 2025 origin of MCP-UI, the creators' prior affiliations (Salomon at Palo Alto Networks, Yosef at Shopify), and the vision that complex websites will decompose into fragmented UI parts consumed through MCP.

resources.title: Liad Yosef — Orply
resources.why: Liad Yosef is co-founder and CTO of Ora, co-creator of MCP Apps, and collaborator on MCP-UI

resources.title: MCP Apps and the future of software inside AI agents
resources.why: MCP-UI was created by Ido Salomon and Liad Yosef in May 2025; Yosef is currently at a stealth startup funded by Sequoia Capital
